label: intended
prompt:
MySQL foreign keys can carry an index name (ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)), but sqlglot does not parse the name. Named foreign keys should parse and round-trip, also when written after a bare CONSTRAINT keyword, which is then dropped.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expecting (. Line 1, Col: 32.
# expected:  ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)

parse_one("ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expecting (. Line 1, Col: 43.
# expected:  ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.

prompt:
MySQL foreign keys can carry an index name (ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)), but sqlglot does not parse the name. Named foreign keys should parse and round-trip, also when written after a bare CONSTRAINT keyword, which is then dropped.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expecting (. Line 1, Col: 32.
# expected:  ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)

parse_one("ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)", read="mysql").sql("mysql")
# currently: ParseError: Expecting (. Line 1, Col: 43.
# expected:  ALTER TABLE t ADD FOREIGN KEY fk (a) REFERENCES p (a)
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
